Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 32424 of 2023
Applicant :- Simraan
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And 3 Others
Counsel for Applicant :- Dileep Kumar Yadav
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Gunjan Sharma
Hon'ble Rajeev Misra,J.

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Heard Mr. Dileep Kumar Yadav, the learned counsel for applicant, the learned A.G.A. for State and Mrs. Gunjan Sharma, the learned counsel representing opposite party-3.

This application for bail has been filed by applicant-Simraan seeking his enlargement on bail in Case Crime No.121 of 2023, under Sections 363, 366, 376, 313, 120-B IPC and Section 3/4 Pocso Act,
police station South, district Firozabad, during the pendency of trial.
Perused the record.
At the very outset, learned A.G.A. submits that notice of the present application for bail has been served upon first informant-opposite party-4 on 17.07.2023.

However, in spite of service of notice,

sentences.text: no one has put in appearance on behalf of first informant-opposite party-4 to oppose this application for bail.

Record shows that in respect of an incident which is alleged to have occurred on 25.03.2021, a delayed F.I.R. dated 27.02.2023 was lodged by first informant, namely, Smt. Bushra (mother of the prosecutrix) and was registered as Case Crime No.0121 of 2023, under Sections 363, 376, 313, 120-B IPC and Section 3/4 Pocso Act, police station South, district Firozabad.
In the aforesaid F.I.R., five persons, namely, Simraan; Nisar Ali; Sahil; Smt. Guddi and Dr. Ragini Agrawal have been nominated as named accused.
Learned counsel for the applicant contends that though applicant is a named and charge-sheeted accused, yet he is liable to be enlarged on bail.
The occurrence giving rise to the present criminal proceedings is alleged to have occurred on 25.03.2021, whereas the F.I.R. was lodged on 27.02.2023.

As such, there is a delay of almost two years in lodging the F.I.R. Since the delay in lodging the F.I.R. has not been sufficiently explained either in the F.I.R. or in the statement of first informant recorded under Section 161 CrPC therefore

, by virtue of the law laid down by the Apex Court in P. Rajagopal Vs. The State of Tamil Nadu AIR 2019 SC 2866 (paragraph 8), the criminal proceedings itself cannot be maintained against the applicant.

entities.text: P. Rajagopal Vs. The State of Tamil Nadu AIR 2019 SC 2866 (paragraph 8)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is then contended by the learned counsel for applicant that it is an admitted case of the prosecution as unfolded in the F.I.R. itself that the prosecutrix has solemnized marriage (Nikah)
with the applicant.
In view of above, the criminality alleged against the applicant cannot be said to have been committed by him.

The police report under Section 173(2) CrPC has already been submitted against four of the named accused including applicant on 02.04.2023, whereas one of the named accused, namely, Dr. Ragini Agrawal has been exculpated.
As such, the entire evidence sought to be relied upon by the prosecution against applicant stands crystalized.
Up to this stage, no such circumstance has emerged necessitating the custodial arrest of the applicant.
Even otherwise, the applicant is a man of clean antecedents having no criminal history to his credit except the present one.
The applicant is in jail since 18.03.2023, as such he has undergone six months of incarceration.
He, therefore, submits that the applicant is liable to be enlarged on bail.
In case the applicant is enlarged on bail, he shall not misuse the liberty of bail and shall co-operate with the trial.
Per contra, the learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the prayer for bail.

He submits that in compliance of the order dated 07.08.2023 passed by this Court, Investigating Officer has collected some material in consonance with the provisions contained in Section 94 of The Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015.

entities.text: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The said material has been brought on record by means of compliance affidavit filed by learned A.G.A. in Court today.

Attention of the Court was then invited to the certificate issued by the Principal, Composite Vidyalaya, Nagla Kirat, City area,
Mainpuri.
As per the said certificate issued by the Principal of said institution, the date of birth of the prosecutrix as recorded in the school record is 16.05.2005.
The occurrence giving rise to the present criminal proceeding occurred on 25.03.2021.
As such, the prosecutrix was aged about 16 years 02 months and 20 days on the date of occurrence.

Attention of the Court was invited to the Simraan vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 18 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73780395/
2 application filed by first informant before the Station House Office/Inspector, police station South,
district Firozabad, wherein it has categorically been stated that certificate which has been issued by the Principal of the institution, copy of which has been brought on record as Annexure-CA-1 of compliance affidavit, is the same institution which was first attended by the prosecutrix.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On the above premise, the learned A.G.A. submits that the prosecutrix was a young girl of tender age on the date of occurrence.

According to the learned A.G.A. though there is a recital in the F.I.R. that forcibly marriage (Nikah) was solemnized by the applicant with the prosecutrix but the applicant himself has failed to bring on record any document that marriage (Nikah) was got solemnized between the parties.

With regard to the delay in lodging of the F.IR., the learned A.G.A. invited the attention of the Court to the F.I.R. itself and on basis of recital contained therein he submits that the delay in lodging the F.I.R. has been duly explained.
On the above premise, he submits that the applicant does not deserve any indulgence by this Court.
The applicant is guilty of dislodging the modesty of the prosecutrix repeatedly and continuously who was admittedly below 18 years of age on the date of occurrence.
As such, no sympathy be shown by this court in favour of the applicant.
The offence complained of is not private in nature but a crime against society.
In fact, the crime committed by applicant falls in the category of moral turpitude.
As such, no good ground has been made out to enlarge the applicant on bail.
When confronted with above, the learned counsel for applicant could not overcome the same.

Having heard the learned counsel for applicant, the learned A.G.A. for State, upon perusal of material brought on record, nature and gravity of offence, evidence, complicity of the accused,
accusation made coupled with the fact that there is nothing on record on the basis of which the credibility or reliability of the prosecutrix could be doubted, the statements of the prosecutrix recorded under Sections 161/164 CrPC clearly establish the complicity of the applicant in the crime in question, no such material has been brought on record on the basis of which it can be inferred that the prosecution of the applicant is false or malicious, the submissions urged by the learned A.G.A. in opposition to the present application for bail could not be dislodged by the learned counsel for applicant with reference to the record at this stage therefore irrespective of the submissions urged by the learned counsel for applicant in support of the bail application but, without making any comment on the merits of the case, this Court does not find any good ground to enlarge the applicant on bail.
This application for bail thus fails and is liable to be rejected.
It is accordingly rejected.

Order Date :- 18.9.2023.
